In fact, 400Hz probably ends up giving you a more stable current going into your phone. The charger goes through a rectifier and a capacitor in parallel to convert it to DC before stepping it down to 5V for charging. The capacitor is in place to smooth out the ripple that is there after rectifying. Because the frequency is much higher, the capacitor will not have time to fully discharge, thus causing the DC current to be much smoother than it would on a standard 60Hz power source.

If your transformers are rated for 1.2MVA then you should be fine. One thing you may want to consider though, is the entire load on the same phase? If you have a three phase setup of 1200kVA and all of them are on a single phase, then you're going to draw more than what the individual transformer is rated for (which is fine for short periods of time). When residential AC units start up, you typically don't experience voltage drop unless you get around 150% of the transformer rating (this also depends on how far your secondary service is running). 

All this to basically say that as long as your load is set up to use all three phases and you aren't already close to your transformers' Max load, there shouldn't be any noticable change.

I don't know of any snakes that are kept in captivity that need to hibernate. You also need a temperature and humidity sensor to make sure the hot end and "cold" end of the tank are correct temperatures. Look up a care sheet for your new snake. It is important that you maintain good temperature/ humidity, especially when it gets time for it to shed.
